want.who_she_is: Marnie Kesh, 39. Her name is on the front of the arcade on the Ellinbay seafront in eight-foot letters, and has been since she married into it at seventeen; she had Ewan at fifteen, before the name. Her husband Denny has been inside four years for what he did in the arcade's back room with the arcade's money. She lives in the flat over it. What she has to lose is the version of her the town agreed on years ago -- the one who held it together, who is coping, who is fine -- and every hour spent being wanted instead of relied on spends some of it.
want.appetite: To be wanted -- not needed, not thanked, not worried about -- by the people she raised or reared. It cannot complete: the direction is what matters. At the start she goes to them; every rung is one of them coming to her instead, and each can come one notch further in. Release 41 adds a door on the front, a relative back for the winter because the season went badly somewhere else, or another hour of the day that belongs to her.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: she goes to them. Flask to the yard because Ewan will not stop for lunch; up the stairs over the chip shop and knock and wait; coat on in her own flat because the meter costs three pounds. Everything she does here she does on her way somewhere else. TOP: they come to her. The arcade after close is where they end up and the flat above it is where they stay; she does not knock at the terrace house and Roan does not lock the back door; the meter runs; whatever she is doing when they arrive is what they walk into. The ascent is PER-PERSON, not global -- a declared fork per the-meters.md W1, because this game declares who_climbs = 'cast'. There is no corruption bar. The four ladders are the four people, each a different kind of going further: Ewan `hold` (how much of her he is allowed to decide -- priced, never courted), Tam `ease` + `want` (how long he can be in a room with her without a reason), Roan `bond` (how much of who she was before is allowed back), Nessa `trust` then `want` (how much of the flat above the arcade is hers to walk into).

decisions.note: Premise chosen to break a copied skeleton, not for novelty. Three of five existing v2 games (back_home, the_allowance, seventh_day) are the same shape: young woman at the bottom of a household, world = interior, family men above her. the-map.md R0 names this in its own text -- 'the only two whose map starts indoors are those two' -- and SKILL.md's operating rule says an example is copied harder than a rule is read. Off Season inverts all three declared axes at once: she is the ELDER (mother/sister/aunt), map.archetype = street_mesh with the exterior as root, who_climbs = 'cast'. Cost: a roster game is more expensive to author than a ladder game (four ladders instead of one).

Cast fixed by LO: 3 male blood + 1 female blood -- Ewan 24 (son), Tam 19 (son), Roan 36 (brother), Nessa 21 (niece). All four blood; one f/f arc. Nessa is tenant #1 of the arcade back room, which is the ROTATING SLOT, so the rotation mechanism is proven from release 1. An outsider (Dov, the pier) was the runner-up and is deferred to 0.2 as the proof that the exterior is a renewable cast source.

Income fixed by LO: the arcade PLUS winter turnarounds on the empty holiday lets. Two work surfaces and two sink locations, which the-economy.md R2 requires (a game passed the sinks gate at 21:20 while twelve of its sinks sat on one front desk). The lets also put her alone in other people's rooms on a schedule, which is the ground the TRIGGERED layer and the walk-in join are built from.

who_climbs = 'cast' with ascent_tiers = [] -- NO player ascent bar at all. the-meters.md W1: the field splits 8 roster / 9 ladder with nothing between 15% and 65%, family games sit on the roster side, and 14 of 25 shipped sandboxes have no player ascent tier. state.md says an empty list is a legitimate declaration for a cast game. Consequence: _school_split (gates.py:1225) counts the player side as ONLY what board.ascent_tiers names, so with [] the cast side should read ~100% and gate 34 passes. Cost: four ladders to author instead of one, and gate 10 falls back to a top-3 heuristic headline -- to be checked at the board gate run before any prose exists.

Per-character meters live on the NPC as [[npcs]] core_traits, read as subject = 'npc' + npc_id + trait_key. NOT as player traits named tam_want. _school_split counts only subject = 'npc' predicates on the cast side, so the prefixed-player-trait form would score 0% cast and fail gate 34 -- the exact gate this game's differentiator rests on.

FOUR DISTINCT METER SHAPES across the cast, on purpose. the-meters.md W6: all five previous v2 games shipped one shape (relation + lust on everybody) and the_allowance gave two of five characters a full pair with zero gate sites. Here: Ewan = one meter + money + a flag (leverage), Tam = two (slow burn, the spine), Roan = one with many rungs (peer/courtship), Nessa = two but STAGED, the second dead until a milestone. Reserving the rich pair for Tam and Nessa follows W6's 'do not gold-plate every character'.

NO counterweight meter. the-meters.md W5: one field game in 25 has one that gates anything, and four of our five shipped one that gates almost nothing (count 0 reads, standing 2, grace 5, propriety 25 reads that are all prose bands). Declining rather than taking one because the template offered one.

MAP CORRECTION made during authoring, against the plan's own diagram. The plan drew the three streets cross-linking (the_front - harbour_end - terrace_row - back to the_front). engine.md 10: navigation_order may list CHILDREN ONLY and the validator hard-fails a sibling link ('includes X which is not a destination'). So harbour_end and terrace_row both hang off the_front and you cross the Front to get between them -- which is what a seafront town actually is, and it makes the exterior more load-bearing rather than less. The graph is a tree rooted on the exterior; the_front carries no entry_from, which is what gate 28 checks.

Every need condition is written in the POSITIVE form -- `warmth gte 30` on the rung that IS offered, never `warmth lt 30` on a rung that is hidden. gates.py:1990: gate 10's direction test walks EVERY player trait, declared or not, and fails any whose lt/lte gates outnumber its gte/gt as 'a descent wearing an ascent's clothes'. Hidden loop traits are exempt only when hidden = true in [[traits.labels]].

Traversal heat is a build requirement, not a nice-to-have: gate 5 needs 60% of DECLARED locations to carry a REPEATABLE canvas with an explicit cycling pool (pool_dir matching _t4|_t5|/sex/). Seven of ten are budgeted hot -- the four hubs, the arcade, the flat and the lets -- which is 70%. The three streets are deliberately cold; the reference game had no sexual content in 8 of its 25 locations.

SILENT DEFECT, caught by the BUILD and by no gate: I wrote choice-level effects as `[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices.config]`. On a CHOICE the keys sit DIRECTLY on the choice — v1.py:1731 reads `choice.flagEffects` and :10445 validates that same path; `config` is the node-level shape for a `type = "location"` exit_block only. 24 blocks were affected, so the warmth grant, the hunger grant and every loop-state reset in the game were valid TOML, parsed clean, and did nothing. Same family as engine.md §21b: a number that never changes looks exactly like a number the player has not moved yet. Fixed by flattening all 24; verified in the BUILT html (entity-encoded, per §24.4 — grepping the raw form finds nothing and that is not a bug signal).

Gate 26 taught the same lesson four times and it is worth stating once: A BRAKE IS RESOLVED ON THE ROUTE INTO A CANVAS. A located, repeatable, room-reachable canvas has no brake on that route, so `costs` on a choice INSIDE it prices nothing. Four surfaces had to be restructured into triggerless rungs behind a priced choice — both arcade takes, the lets turnaround, the meter, the eat, and the solo loop. Tam's loop was already that shape, which is exactly why his meters were never flagged and the others' were.

AND THE COUNTERPART, which pulls the other way: engine.md §16 requires a flag read by a trigger to be SET FROM A LOCATED CANVAS. Moving the meter's grant to a triggerless rung took `meter_fed_once` with it and hard-failed the build. The two requirements are not the same requirement and must be split: the FLAG stays on the located canvas, the GRANT moves behind the price.

THREE METERS STARTED ABOVE THEIR OWN GATE — warmth 40 vs a gate at 30, energy 100 vs 20, hunger 60 vs 25 — so every door those needs were supposed to shut was open from turn one at zero clicks (gate 26). Fixed by starting her below each: warmth 18, energy 16, hunger 20. It is better fiction as well: the first Monday is now a real choice between the counter and a turnaround, and the first three pounds in the meter is the thing that opens the flat.

THE DAY-CAP FLAG NOW SITS ON THE CHOICE, NOT THE RUNG'S EXIT -- 14 moved, and this is the placement rule for everything authored here from now on. The generator emits the two in opposite orders: a CHOICE runs flagEffects -> costs -> ... -> advanceTime (v2.py:12648-12733); a NODE EXIT runs advanceTime -> traitEffects -> flagEffects (v2.py:13085-13088). advanceTime rolls the day inside itself (v2.py:5411-5414) and advanceDay is where [engine.daily_tick] clears every _today flag (v2.py:5552). So an exit-set cap on a rung that crosses midnight is written on the FAR SIDE of the clear and the new day starts already capped. Measured here: act_flat_sleep ran 21:00-06:00, so from night two onward Sleep was never offered before midnight again and the player was pushed into a permanent post-midnight bedtime; rung_roan_stay, rung_roan_later, rung_nessa_tea and rung_nessa_curtain sat in the same trap on late hub windows. Placement scan after: exit-set 15 -> 0, choice-set 0 -> 18 (14 rungs + the four talk caps from D1). act_flat_sleep lost `slept_today` ENTIRELY rather than moving it -- it is a LOCATED canvas, so its max_triggers_per_day = 1 is a real cap and markCanvasTriggered stamps the day key BEFORE advanceTime (v2.py:4290), and the 21:00-06:00 window is end-exclusive besides (v2.py:3790-3810). SKILL HALF SHIPPED THE SAME DAY, because the-meters.md M5's worked example is where this came from: M5 now sets the flag on the choice, engine.md 28 is rewritten (its old warning at :989 said the cap gets CLEARED, which the emit order makes impossible), and a new gate `a day-cap closes` holds the three-part shape. The measurement that settles it: 78 day caps in this repo already sit on the choice against 40 on an exit, and 35 of those 40 belong to off_season and the_allowance -- the two games written under that example.

FOURTEEN references remain in the game and every one is a rota or a rule -- this game runs on rotas (a chip shop, a boat yard, an arcade with opening hours) and C2 exempts a rule by design, so 17.6 per 10k against a field median of 1.1 is the correct end state, not a remaining defect. The test is the LIST, not the rate.

TWO LINES THAT WERE FALSE ON AN AXIS THE DOCTRINE DID NOT NAME. T4: hub_ewan_yard opened with 'It's not Monday. What's gone wrong?' and his yard row is weekdays [0..5] where 0 IS Monday -- the first line of his hub was wrong once a week from the day it was written. Now 'You don't come down here. What's gone wrong?', same beat, no claim about the day. T5: 'Forty-one pounds sixty. The pitch is ninety. It is Thursday.' had three faults in one sentence -- a currency name, a day wrong six times in seven in an all-days canvas, and a FIGURE THE SIDEBAR WAS ALREADY PRINTING CORRECTLY BESIDE IT. Now 'Whatever the figure is, it is not ninety. It has not been ninety since the clocks went back.' SKILL HALF: the-clock.md C2 was written about the HOUR only; it now carries the same reading-versus-rule test on two more axes -- the day of the week, and any figure the state already holds -- stated generally as 'a beat may not state anything the engine is already tracking', with a plain warning that the lint sees neither axis and a human has to.

NESSA'S HUB WINDOWED TO 12:00-15:00, AND THE COST OF THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. She has TWO back-room rows -- 22:00-08:00 'asleep behind the curtain' and 12:00-15:00 'on her phone' -- and a portrait hub with no schedule renders across both, so an opener saying she is awake and speaking was wrong for 10 of the 13 hours she is present. There is no fix inside one canvas: the engine has no time-of-day CONDITION type (trait / flag / item / pass / npc_at_location / clothing_* / worn_*, v2.py:7736-7844), so a [group] cannot band an opener on the clock. A portrait hub does honour a schedule -- selectNpcPortraitCanvasesForLocation runs each candidate through isCanvasValid (v2.py:4482-4498). CONSEQUENCE, ACCEPTED: her arc is now reachable in a 3-hour daily window and her night presence has NO surface at all. That is the-surfaces.md R1 saying a canvas is MISSING, not that this one should widen -- the night hub is content and belongs with the empty rooms (REVIEW_1 P1/P2), and it is the first thing the rooms batch should write. A true line in a short window beats a false one in a long one.

THE CLOCK LINT'S BLIND SPOTS WERE HIDING OUR DEFECTS AND ALMOST NONE OF THE FIELD'S -- a skill fix this game paid for. _clk_refs could not see `half nine`, `<hour> in the morning` with no preposition, or an hour followed by `the` ('by nine THE whole flat', killed by the stoplist entry that was there to catch 'at one point'); and it double-counted phrases two patterns both matched. All four fixed, plus span-based dedupe. MEASURED ON THE 25-GAME CORPUS BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN: the correction moves the FIELD from median 1.0 to 1.1 -- one game, one true positive ('gathered at half past six for drinks') -- and moves OURS by a quarter to a half: off_season 20.1 -> 26.4, steam 29.2 -> 36.6, forty_miles 22.6 -> 34.4. The shapes it could not see are ones our authors reach for and the corpus does not. REJECTED with the number that killed it: dropping the allow-list entirely is the tidier rule and inflates the FIELD to 1.2 / 2.6, which is noise being scored -- the instrument deliberately under-counts rather than over-counts, the safe direction for a list nobody scores. FIELD_MEDIAN / FIELD_P75 updated 1.0/2.0 -> 1.1/2.1 and the-clock.md's published table re-measured with the SHIPPED function, not a copy of it.

THE CRUDE CEILING WAS STALE AND THE TABLE MOVED, NOT THE PROSE. the_want.md 6 put 'cum / come in' in the OPENS LATER column for Tam and Ewan while loop_tam_bed.finish already shipped 'he comes in your mouth' and rung_ewan_caravan 'He comes over your knuckles'. The prose is right -- it is under no other ceiling, it is the crudest writing in the game, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a ceiling is never a floor and writing under it is the defect. So the table moved, in the_want.md and here in want.crude_ceiling. A ceiling that lags what shipped is worse than no ceiling, because the next release reads it and writes UNDER it. Also fixed: both meter screens said three buys 'about a day and a half' of warmth against +45 and a decay of 12/day from a base of 18 -- about three days.

REPAIR BATCH 3 -- 'the first hour', 2026-08-22. The first batch that WRITES PROSE, and a redistribution rather than an addition: +565 words net. L2, O1-O4, N1 and N2 closed. THE OPENING IS A COLD OPEN NOW, AND THE CAST MOVED RATHER THAN BEING CUT. the-first-hour.md F1: the field runs two shapes and nothing between them -- a cold open names NOBODY at ~150 words, a staged open spends 700-2,600 putting people on screen one at a time. The defect is the middle, and canvas_opening was the middle: 277 words naming SIX people with none on screen, none speaking, and two of the six not in the game at all -- 46 words per named character against the field's ~229. It is now two nodes, 159 words, ZERO characters named, carrying her situation and the pressure and nothing else. Where the rest went: the building and the ninety to canvas_first_arcade; the four of them to canvas_meet_*, each on screen and speaking. The reversal -- the pitch does not go to a landlord -- is now said by EWAN, IN HIS OWN YARD, instead of asserted at a player who has met nobody. Checked before relying on it: the rent does not fire on day one, because advanceDay() arms the demand when the day rolls TO due_day (engine.md 26) and the game starts ON Monday, so there is a full week to meet him before he appears at the counter.

canvas_first_arcade -- ONE CANVAS, THREE JOBS. (1) It says what the place IS. `amusement arcade`, `slot machine`, `coin pusher`, `change booth` appeared NOWHERE in player-visible prose before it -- only in image_search_queries and image `description`, which renders as the alt attribute (v2.py:13750) and, with no media on disk, not at all. A human read the built game and asked 'what is arcade??' and the game had no answer anywhere in it. (2) It catches the building and the ninety that came out of the cold open, and names the collector by ROLE because the player has not met him (F7). (3) It closes the dead half-hour: a non-repeatable, unscheduled, non-random canvas auto-fires on entry (v2.py:4453) and its own exit spends 30 minutes, so 07:33 -> 08:03 and the player comes out of the introduction with the counter open. The introduction does the waiting. NO SCHEDULE, deliberately -- it has to be live at whatever minute the funnel hands over, and it is about a room rather than a person, so there is no presence to match.

FOUR MEETINGS, FOUR FLAGS, FOUR WINDOWS -- `every hub is met first` 0/4 -> 4/4. The forbidden shape this replaces: a repeatable `npc =` hub whose base node IS the introduction. All four hubs carried NO CONDITION AT ALL, so every portrait was live on turn one and the game had no meeting state at all. canvas_meet_ewan / _tam / _roan / _nessa: 119-135 words each, one node, four dialog blocks, built to the worked shape the_inheritance/canvas_meet_audrey. Each sets ONE FLAG OF ITS OWN -- F8, because seventh_day gated two hubs on `rota_running`, steam two on `doors_open` and back_home FOUR on `arrival_done`, which is the cold-spawn hub with a coat on. NODE NAME IS THE ROLE AND THE HUB'S IS THE NAME (F7): Your eldest -> Ewan, Your youngest -> Tam, Your brother -> Roan, Your sister's girl -> Nessa. The lint `named before met` goes 3 people -> 0, and the_terrace_house's description stopped saying 'Roan' before he is met. NO WAVES, and that is a call rather than an oversight: F8 prefers staggered entrances, but this game's premise is that all four live inside four hundred yards and she is related to every one of them, so gating them by day would be an invented lock on the one thing the world is about.

THE FOUR MILESTONE ONE-SHOTS ARE BOUND TO THEIR CHARACTER'S HOURS NOW (N2). canvas_first_borrow, canvas_tam_saw_you, canvas_roan_back_door and canvas_nessa_saw_her were location-bound with NO schedule and NO requires_npc, so each could auto-fire with its character absent and narrate them into an empty room -- canvas_first_borrow put Ewan at the desk in a yard he left two hours earlier. All four now carry the same window as that character's meeting, plus requires_npc. ⚠️ requires_npc ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT: isCanvasValid (v2.py:4573) checks schedules, conditions and repeatability and never reads that field on the auto-fire path, which is exactly how vesper/cap_renner_hired introduces Renner in an empty bar at ten in the morning. The SCHEDULE is the gate; requires_npc documents intent and is correct on the two paths that do read it (v2.py:5259, :5332). Verified live both ways.

A GATE CAUGHT THIS BATCH ON ITS WAY IN AND THE GATE WAS RIGHT -- recorded because the tempting fix was to weaken it. `milestones open something` failed canvas_first_arcade the moment it existed: a one-shot that sets no flag opens nothing and owes an explanation. Widening the gate to excuse 'first visits' was MEASURED FIRST AND REJECTED -- a blanket sets-nothing exemption would have excused 10 canvases across four games, including six mid-arc capstones in the_inheritance (marg_move_staff, marg_cap_velvet, aud_wave2_richard...) and three in vesper (captivity_intro, salvage_chip_snag...) that it is correctly catching. A narrower 'exempt whatever `the opening opens a door` counted as the door' variant was also measured and would still have wrongly excused the_inheritance/marg_move_staff, because _fh_live_at ignores conditions. SO THE CANVAS CHANGED INSTEAD, AND THE CHANGE IS BETTER GAME DESIGN: the three arcade work bands gated on `season_shut`, A FLAG SET UPSTAIRS IN HER FLAT, so the counter was workable in a building whose shutter was still down. They now gate on `shutter_up`, set by canvas_first_arcade. The funnel became a real chain (flat -> arcade -> the counter opens) and the gate went green on its own terms rather than by exemption. work_lets_turnaround KEEPS season_shut: the holiday lets are not behind that shutter, and the SEASON being shut is what makes winter turnarounds her work.

THE DIESEL SINK EXISTS NOW, AND IT IS THE ONLY RUNG WHERE MONEY BUYS A METER. board.economy.sinks has carried 'diesel for the van - harbour_end - $12' since 0.1 and it could not be built, because harbour_end had no canvas that could spend anything. It is rung_ewan_diesel, a CHOICE ON THE SLIP HUB rather than a solo activity -- deliberate: a solo repeatable canvas plus a scheduled NPC makes a location qualify for the walk-in floor (_walkin_join in gates.py) and harbour_end has no walk-in, while a portrait hub carries `npc` and does not qualify a room. $12 -> +4 hold, day-capped. Money as the brake AND the point: the_want.md gives Ewan `hold` alone -- 'priced, never courted' -- so paying into him IS the climb, and this is the only place in the game that is true. show_when_blocked SHIPPED -- THE FIRST USE OF THE PRIMITIVE ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO. REPAIR BATCH 5 -- 'the act loops', 2026-08-22. G1 closed and promises[0] PAID. Scoreboard 37/38 held; this batch is scored by the lints rather than the gates: the act menu goes 2 loops / 6 cascades -> 5 loops / 3 cascades, and `ends on an opening` goes 1 visible-locked choice -> 4, one 0.2 door per character. the_want.md 6 says the crude register lives in 'the act loops on the four hubs' and ONE of the four existed; Ewan, Roan and Nessa each had a five-beat cascade -- a scene replaying identically on a surface the player is meant to live in (the-surfaces.md R3b). THE CEILING TABLE ANSWERED EVERY DESIGN QUESTION IN THIS BATCH, read as what the ACTS reach rather than as a word list. the_want.md 6 puts `fuck` in the 0.1 column for Tam and Roan and `cunt` in Ewan's OPENS LATER column -- and the build had no penetration anywhere, which is CLAUDE.md's 'writing under the ceiling is the defect'. So: Tam and Roan top out at penetration; EWAN'S LADDER IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL IN 0.1 because his 0.1 cannot reach her, so `fuck` there is the verb and not the act and his rungs are what she does to him; Nessa tops out at fingers and tongue because `fuck` is in her later column. Each character's 0.2 door is then drawn from their own later column: arse / his hand on her cunt / come inside / let her fuck you. A HAND AUDIT of every crude term in all four loops against that character's own 0.1 column found ZERO breaches -- a check no gate performs and the one the want exists for.

promises[0] PAID, NOT DEFERRED AGAIN. Tam's two locked doors WERE penetration, which his 0.1 column permits. Batch 1 capped his want at 60 purely to hold them shut and wrote into this ledger: '0.2 MUST RAISE THE CAP IN THE SAME CHANGE that builds the content behind those doors.' Batch 5 is that change -- cap 60 -> 85, both doors route into a real `astride` act node, and the finisher gained a stage-3 band. Leaving it locked while Roan penetrated would also have made the want's own answer false ('Which repeatable surface carries the crudest writing? Tam's act loop'), which is the one thing that file is checked against. His new 0.2 door is `arse` at want >= 90, unreachable against the 85 cap -- the G2 lesson applied by construction rather than by hope.

TWO THINGS THE BATCH FOUND ABOUT ITSELF. (1) `somebody speaks` hit EXACTLY 5.0:1 against a 5.0 ceiling mid-batch: the act nodes had gone voiceless, which register.md S3 forbids outright ('if a person is in the room, they speak'). Eight act nodes were given a line each and it settled at 4.8:1. A batch of pure explicit prose is precisely the one that pushes that ratio and the ceiling is what caught it. (2) The ceiling audit exposed that the 0.2 DOORS were inconsistent -- Tam's named its act plainly while the other three hedged ('tell her what is in the bottom of your wardrobe'). A locked door is a SIGNPOST, not content, and the-voice.md R4 wants the greyed row to state the want, because a want is what sells the next release. All four now name it plainly. PIVOT DIAGNOSTIC on all 25 explicit beats across the four loops: 25 on the body, 0 pivots.

THREE CASCADES LEFT AS CASCADES, ON PURPOSE. walkin_flat_stairs is a substitution router branch and the-surfaces.md R3 sizes those at 'one or two paragraphs plus a media pool' -- DoL's are 458-473 bytes -- and warns that writing a full encounter each time 'is how this rule dies'. work_arcade_after_close's floor beat is solo texture at a location whose solo loop already exists upstairs in the flat. rung_tam_nothing is the stair TO Tam's loop, not a surface beside it. R3b's own line -- 'one good loop beats four thin ones' -- cuts against converting any of the three, and the act-menu lint is explicitly A COUNT, NEVER A TARGET.

REPAIR BATCH 6 -- 'the words the player has to already own', 2026-08-22. L1, L3, M3 and G3 closed. 6 open -> 1 open, 33 fixed. Scoreboard 37/38 held and `location fill` is now the ONLY red gate in the game. This was LO's FIRST complaint and the last one still open: 'the language being used here is tough to get... why couldnt we use simpler language'. A WORD-BY-WORD JUDGEMENT, NOT A PURGE, because the lint's own docstring forbids chasing the number: 'the rate does not discriminate... what separates them is what the words ARE'. The list went 94 words / 203 uses -> 63 / 121; ambiguous 3 -> 0; false friends 3 -> 1. Player-visible hits remaining: ZERO, checked with the lint's own _player_visible_text rather than a grep -- the media description fields still say 'settee' and 'jumper' and SHOULD, because they are find-media search hints and not prose.

THE THREE KINDS OF FIX, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT. FALSE FRIENDS (the worst kind -- they do not look like jargon so the reader silently misreads): vest -> T-shirt, jumper -> sweater. SWAPPED for the plain word: settee, telly, mam, hoover, eiderdown, hob, fortnight, snooker, rota, lodger. GLOSSED ON FIRST USE per register.md, because the object is doing work and deleting it would flatten the room: 'an immersion heater for the hot water', 'the chip shop's extractor fan', 'a chandlery -- the shop that sells boat parts', 'a coin mechanism'. AMBIGUOUS: half three -> half past three. LEFT: `tea` stays on the list and IS A FALSE POSITIVE -- eleven of its twelve uses are the drink ('two teas in the two mugs he owns', 'a tea towel') and only 'they all go home for their tea' was the meal, which moved. The 63 words remaining are number words the corpus never spells, proper nouns the fiction teaches, coinages, and plain English the 25 games happen not to use (arithmetic, diesel, barometer, kettle) -- named in REVIEW_1 so nobody 'fixes' them later.

A CURRENCY REGRESSION I WROTE MYSELF, AND THE LINT HOLE THAT HID IT. Batch 2 declared a neutral '$' and stripped pounds/quid/euros. Batches 4 and 5 put British COIN units back: fifties x6, 'sixty pence', 'the two-pence one', 'to the penny' -- THREE OF THEM IN CANVASES WRITTEN DURING THIS REPAIR, matching the surrounding British texture instead of the declared rule. Six fifties for a $3 charge is arithmetic nonsense. And `the currency in the prose` said 'no beat names a currency' the whole time, because gates.py's _CUR_UNIT knew pound/dollar/euro/yen and NO SUB-UNITS. Both halves fixed: the words are gone from the game, and the lint learned pence/penny/cent with a `per cent` guard that was MEASURED first (without it, steam's 'the trade is down forty per cent' false-positives twice). Red before green -- the corrected lint printed both mismatch warnings, then went clean. Repo-wide it newly and correctly flags forty_miles' 'fifty-pence tube'; no gate moved on any game. This is the 'an example teaches' failure aimed at myself.

Six of the seven hosts use PATTERN B (exclusive_group): one roll split into cumulative buckets (v2.py:5361-5379), so the substitution rate is the sum of the chances instead of 1 - prod(1 - p). solo_flat_warm deliberately stays PATTERN A -- groups are processed BEFORE independent rules (v2.py:5359), so a group there would take 22% off Tam's band before it rolled, and him coming up the stairs is the flat's headline content; the two new branches are declared after his bands and only roll when he misses.

The lint also prints the host's own survival odds, because Pattern A vs Pattern B is invisible in the TOML and decides whether the odds an author wrote are the odds that run. It found back_home's activity_wash rendering itself 24% of the time, and it found a latent defect in THIS game: solo_flat_warm's three bands are described as one-of-three and the first one only said `ease lt 20`, which is satisfied at the same time as `want gte 22` -- two of three live, canvas rendering 11%. map.shape: Ellinbay seafront in February. THE FRONT is the ground and the root -- the promenade everything opens onto. Three ways off it: the arcade (with the back room behind and her flat above), the holiday lets, and two streets, HARBOUR END (the working end, the boat yard) and TERRACE ROW (the residential street, the chip shop flat and their mother's terrace house). You cross the Front to get between the two streets, which is what a seafront town actually is.
map.r1_signoff: OWED -- unsigned. LO to walk the graph and sign with a date before 0.1 ships. the-map.md: an author signing off their own map is not a sign-off, and that is exactly what the 26/26 house-shaped game recorded.

locations.job: Her ground and the only place in Ellinbay with her name on it. She comes here because it is where she is when nothing is happening -- the change bag, the machines that eat pound coins, the counter you can see the whole front from.
Home base. Two rings, an immersion, a meter that wants three pounds, and a window over a sea nobody comes to see. Where she sleeps, warms up, and is alone.
THE ROTATING SLOT. Behind the arcade, where Denny did what he did. Forty a week, a mattress, a curtain instead of a door. Nessa's now.
Ewan's, and where the lease and the arcade's books live in a drawer he keeps shut. She comes here to ask, which is the whole problem.
Tam's -- up the outside stair over the fryers, hot in a town where nothing else is. The spine of 0.1. Also the only hot food on the front in February.
Their mother's old place, Roan's now. The one room in Ellinbay that remembers her as somebody's daughter instead of somebody's mother.
Six holiday flats above the front, empty from October. She does the winter turnarounds on a key -- alone, in a room that is not hers, on a schedule other people know.
The promenade, and the ground the whole town sits on. Everything opens onto it and you cross it to get anywhere. Shuttered, wind off the water, one bin lorry.
The working end of the front -- trailers, a slip, diesel. The one part of Ellinbay that still has a reason to be open in February.
The street behind the front where the people who live here actually live. Chip shop at one end, their mother's house at the other.
